close_reason: opinion: 6 bools are intentional RFC 5280 policy switches; no safety gain from refactor
description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:510 (ValidationPolicy struct)

Clippy pedantic flags this as 'more than 3 bools in a struct'. ValidationPolicy has 6 boolean fields:

  enforce_key_usage: bool,
  initial_explicit_policy: bool,
  initial_any_policy_inhibit: bool,
  initial_policy_mapping_inhibit: bool,
  require_subject_alt_name: bool,
  require_rfc822_san: bool,

This is a design-level flag: many booleans in a struct are a sign that some of them may be better grouped or represented as a bitflags-style type, or that the struct is accumulating policy concerns it should delegate.

Whether to act on this is a judgment call. The current layout is intentional and well-documented. However, the flag should be acknowledged: if any new bool policies are added, the cluster of booleans grows and callers face combinatorial confusion about which flags interact.

A bitflags wrapper for the three RFC 5280 §6.1.1 inhibit/initial flags (initial_explicit_policy, initial_any_policy_inhibit, initial_policy_mapping_inhibit) would reduce the bool count without breaking callers.
title: [rusty] pkix-path: ValidationPolicy has more than 3 bools (clippy::struct_excessive_bools)
